# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection

**Evidence:** `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (15,512 frames, ~4h21m capture). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory.

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 (LAN: 10.2.28.0/24) |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad (Intel) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR |
| Logged-in domain user | `EASYAS123\brolf` (Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, confirmed twice: to DC 10.2.28.2 and via NBNS) |
| AD domain | easyas123.tech, DC EASYAS123-DC (10.2.28.2) |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (NetSupport Manager remote-access tool abused as a RAT). **Signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral:
- HTTP requests carry literal header `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`
- Server responses carry literal header `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`
- Application-layer protocol matches the known NetSupport C2 exchange exactly: `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1` client beacons answered with `CMD=ENCD / ES=1 / DATA=<encrypted blob>` (frames in TCP stream 40, e.g. #2638–#2645 onward).

## Timeline / Infection Vector

- t=44.44s: victim's browser resolves and visits `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (23.64.147.24) over TLS.
- t=44.77s–44.81s: two DNS queries for `vadusa.xyz` fail to resolve, then succeed (frame 2566) resolving to **45.131.214.85**.
- t=45.05s: first C2 POST beacon fires to `45.131.214.85` — under 1 second after resolution.

This sequence (legitimate government-site visit immediately followed by resolution of a throwaway `.xyz` domain and instant RAT beaconing) is consistent with a malvertising/compromised-page redirect chain delivering the NetSupport RAT payload; no separate binary download was captured over HTTP in this pcap (delivery either happened via HTTPS to the redirector or via a mechanism not visible in cleartext).

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `45.131.214.85:443` (plaintext HTTP over TCP/443, not TLS) — sole C2 endpoint, single persistent TCP session (stream 40, victim port 51912), 264 POST beacons over the full ~4.36-hour capture (t=45.05s to t=15682.04s), steady `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` keep-alive pattern.
- C2 URL: `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm`

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` → resolves to 45.131.214.85 (DNS frame #2566)

**Other observed domain of interest (pre-infection, likely lure/redirector):**
- `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (23.64.147.24) — visited via TLS one second before the malicious DNS lookup; content not visible (encrypted), flagged as part of the infection chain based on timing.

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None recoverable. No executable, script, or file object was transferred in cleartext HTTP; C2 traffic body is `DATA=` fields that are encrypted/obfuscated (`ES=1` = encryption enabled in the NetSupport gateway protocol), so no file names or SHA256 hashes can be extracted from this capture.

## Recommended Action

Isolate DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88) from the network immediately, block 45.131.214.85 and `vadusa.xyz` at the perimeter/DNS sinkhole, and perform host-based forensics (disk/memory) to recover the dropped NetSupport client binary and installation persistence mechanism, since none of that is visible in network traffic alone.
